reviews.text: Terrible doctors. If you don't want your pet to die, don't bring them here. They couldn't even perform an ultrasound or give a proper diagnosis.

We had a consultation with Dr. Mayra Lazaro, a veterinary gastroenterologist. Fortunately, we were lucky enough to find an opening in her schedule, as our dog had been sick for several days and no other veterinarian could identify his condition. Dr. Lazaro treated him professionally and personally, prescribing a treatment that worked immediately. Thankfully, he is feeling much better, and we are grateful for the care and service provided by both the clinic and Dr. Lazaro. 🐶🐶
They denied me service and have been refusing to schedule an appointment for me for over two weeks.

Three years ago, I came to this center, and I believe they saved my dog ​​from an illness that other places couldn't treat properly for nine months.

For the past year, I've taken my dog ​​here, and they always ask me questions that are clearly in her medical record. For the last six months, they haven't been able to properly diagnose my dog ​​here. At eight years old, they just say it's because she's a geriatric patient. My dog ​​isn't getting better.
Thank you so much for your review.
Thank you for your review.

Terrible "high-specialty" service. They take advantage of the owner's desperation.

I went to 10 veterinarians before coming here, hoping they could help my dog.

Their website boasts: "We are the first Veterinary Hospital in Mexico with a specialty area for treating pets with gastrointestinal conditions, staffed by the DVM, who is the second subspecialist in Gastroenterology in Mexico (a higher level than the specialty)."

The outrageous reality is that the subspecialist NEVER showed up to check on my dog ​​during the three appointments he had. The service feels like a game of telephone with her team; it must be the hospital's protocol, but she's a ghost (maybe because she's busy with more important things, I don't know).

I handed them the diagnoses for IBD and IPE. They didn't have to waste time investigating; they just had to apply the basic protocols. However, they treated each allergy symptom in isolation (as the months went by, he developed eye discharge and paw problems). Although their website clearly states that gastrointestinal issues can be a manifestation of “allergies, food intolerances,” their team completely ignored their own medical literature.
They should have implemented an elimination diet, but they never suggested it; they preferred to fragment the symptoms by treating them separately instead of recognizing that the entire body was rejecting the allergen.

The most negligent aspect was that they never gave him a Vitamin B12 injection, which is essential and mandatory for a dog with malabsorption. Due to their malpractice, my dog ​​continued to waste away.

In desperation, I sought a second opinion. Just ONE DIRECT CONSULTATION with a competent veterinarian was enough for her to listen to me, see the complete picture, administer his Vitamin B12 immediately, and start him on a hydrolyzed diet with a different brand of food.

In just five days, with this change, by finally removing the allergen, that intestine with IBD—which will always have the disease—was finally able to rest from so much inflammation.

Don't waste your money or risk your pets at this place. They play with people's hopes and charge for a subspecialty that the patient never receives in person.

Many of us come to this place because we're referred by other hospitals or even other doctors, but the truth is, its "fame" is due to its size and large staff. The care leaves much to be desired, especially the patient follow-up. It's clear that many discharges are simply to free up space because it's so crowded. It's like a public hospital with private prices. Since it's divided into several buildings and branches of the same hospital, they tend to pass the buck to each other to get rid of cases that overwhelm them. Honestly, it's better to find a place with more personalized care and not one that operates on a piecemeal basis or by volume, like here. I was very disappointed with this place and the care my dog ​​received today.

BEWARE! They profit, or rather, they ROB animals in a very blatant and cruel way. My cat had very advanced cancer, which was evident in his physical condition and tests, but even so, they told us that the best thing would be to operate. They don't explain the services they charge for, and you're not even sure that everything they charge you for was actually done; there's no proof. Leaving your pet with them is like giving them a blank check. He was only there for a day and a half, and the bill came to over 30,000 pesos!!! And they killed him. Before that, when we visited him, he looked bad, and we wanted to take him home to say goodbye as a family. Even the vet on duty agreed with that decision because he wasn't in a condition for surgery, but she told us to consult with his attending veterinarian, who still insisted. Of course, the surgery cost over 18,000 pesos, and the truth is, they take advantage of people's trust in their supposed "professionalism," assuming they'll recommend the best course of action or something with a certain degree of probability, but in reality, they just want to squeeze as much money out of us as possible. I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT. IT'S VERY BLATANT AND ABOVE ALL CRUEL!!

My dog ​​was seen by several veterinarians, some good and some not. One doctor administered an IV, which was ineffective due to a blood clot that went undetected until the catheter was removed. Because of his pre-existing health conditions and this, the decision was made a few minutes later to euthanize him to prevent further suffering.

Overall, our experience has always been good, although sometimes the reception staff can be a bit slow, which is understandable given they're overwhelmed with time, patients, and questions.

What I can say is that the care we've received for 10 years from Dr. Fernando Amaro has been impeccable. His attention, dedication, and vocation are unparalleled. Thank you so much for your support and care.

My dog, Blue Demon, passed away five months ago. I brought him to this HORRID AND EXTREMELY EXPENSIVE PLACE on a recommendation. DON'T DO IT!! Every face I saw in the couple of hours I was there was filled with uncertainty and sadness. Why demand a deposit? Excuse me, but if I were taking my friend, my best friend, to a place like this, would I leave him there? They PROFIT from people's pain and desperation. He needed an ultrasound, but they told me it was SCHEDULED. Isn't this supposed to be a HOSPITAL? When we took him to another hospital, they told us the OBVIOUS thing: it couldn't be done. If we had done it that way, I could have understood, and at least he wouldn't have spent his last night ALONE. I sent an email; they were going to contact me. They didn't. NO ONE AND NOTHING IS GOING TO BRING MY DOG BACK TO ME. But I wasn't going to be left with the debt and the eternal feeling that I FAILED him and left him ALONE one night, his last night.

Excellent service from all the staff, very clean, and very organized. It's a top-notch hospital where you know your pets will receive the best care. Having the laboratories and diagnostic equipment on-site is a huge advantage. This makes things much faster and truly makes a difference.

The excellent service I received the first time turned into a terrible experience. They saw my dog ​​for an ophthalmology appointment, and a month later, when I tried to schedule her second appointment, it turned out they had no appointments available after 2 pm. And certainly not on Saturdays or Sundays.
The telephone service provided by Roxana Avila is rude, unhelpful, and incomprehensible. When you ask her to repeat herself, she gets annoyed. As a telephone operator, she should speak more fluently and clearly, or at least have the patience to repeat what she said. In conclusion: I absolutely do not recommend this place.

They scheduled our appointment incorrectly and preferred to kick us out rather than let the doctor see us. Since they have so many patients, it's not like they care about one more dog or one less; it's all the same to them. The staff's service and customer service were terrible. They were supposed to come down here to offer a solution, but nothing. They just kicked us out.
We arrived 10 minutes late for our appointment, and they waited another 20 minutes before telling us that the requested doctor couldn't see us (for some reason, you schedule with your preferred doctor). In short, they do whatever they want. Their scheduling and customer service are awful. They need to get their act together.
Excellent service.
Efficient service.
The care I received was excellent. They operated on my 13-year-old dog to remove a malignant tumor, and he's currently undergoing chemotherapy. Highly recommended.
The best

It's a place that looks nice and clean at first glance, but the truth is, we all go to a veterinarian for the experience, not the aesthetics. I went to the cardiology and gastroenterology department for my dog. I had some questions about a medication, which I asked via WhatsApp, and they only told me they would pass my message on to the doctor. Neither she nor the clinic followed up, and they never contacted me to give me an answer.
I also asked them for help filling out a medical report. The cardiologist took weeks to return it to me, and when she finally did, the dates were incorrect, according to her interpretation. I asked her to correct it, and it took her more than four weeks to send it back. I sent follow-up messages almost daily, and they always told me they were talking to the doctor, who was busy and hadn't had time to review it. They have an organizational problem and terrible customer service. When I gave them this feedback, I felt like it wasn't well received and was met with complete disregard.

Excellent clinic. It's expensive, but in Mexico, costs are high, and you receive quality care. I first visited her with my previous pet, who had a very serious diagnosis, but we finally found out what was wrong in just one appointment. Now I take my cat to Dr. Carolina Ordoñez, and she's excellent. I found him in very bad shape off the street; he has feline HIV, and the first year was very difficult, but today he's completely stable and happy. Now I'll start taking my dog ​​for checkups too, confident that I'll find the same professionalism.
I've recommended her to a couple of people, and they've had great experiences as well.

Terrible place. The so-called doctor, who claims to be a master of skin specialists, never diagnosed my dog's condition in a year, until she ordered a CT scan, and by then it was too late. They admitted her, I spent 50,000 pesos, and it was still too late. It's a terrible place, just a place to rip you off. DON'T GO THERE

Do you love your pets and want exceptional service?

NEVER COME HERE!!

The doctor in charge has no ethics, no values, and no interest in pets. She only cares about your money.

We made an appointment, confirmed it, and she refused to see us because we hadn't been in a year and we arrived late!!

She sent us to a supposed Patient Care Manager, made us wait 35 minutes, and then didn't see us, but of course... they were quick to collect payments.

Mayra, aren't you uncomfortable?

There's someone in your waiting room fighting for the same thing.

May life treat you the way you treat your patients.

I am so grateful to Dr. Mayra, from Gastroenterology, for all the care, follow-up, and excellent results with Monet.

At another hospital, they told me that surgery was necessary to reach a diagnosis. Fortunately, we went to Dr. Mayra, and surgery was never needed. Oral medication, supplements, and a change in diet were enough to treat his problem.

After two months, Monet was discharged without ever needing surgery. 🥹🐾

Thank you so much, Doctor, for your attention, patience, and for taking such good care of Monet.

If your dog has recurring vomiting or diarrhea, don't hesitate to schedule a consultation with her. I highly recommend her. ❤️
Thank you for your review.

Very good doctors, in my experience. We've certainly had a good experience dealing with the staff and doctors. There are waiting rooms and plenty of consulting rooms.

The price per consultation can be a bit high since you're usually dealing with specialists, but the other services are reasonable.

100% recommended for complex issues, but it might be preferable to go to a more general practitioner first before coming here.

I feel it's a good hospital with good doctors, the problem is the bad experience starts at reception. The guy there was very friendly, but the woman was awful; rude, rude, and had terrible communication skills. In short, very poor customer service, and she's the first person you see when you go there.

I asked for information about a urine culture, and all she told me to do was send a WhatsApp message so she could give me the phone number of the doctor who treats my dog.
When I called back to tell her the doctor wasn't answering, I called reception again, and the woman didn't even say good morning. She just put me on hold with music playing, and then the call was cut off without her answering.
In the end, I ended up calling the emergency room, and a very nice and kind doctor named Roxana finally helped me.
Excellent service 🐕‍🦺

My dog ​​went to all three branches (dermatology, emergency, and internal medicine) for five months. Despite numerous tests, they never found anything wrong. Every time he got sick, they told me to bring him in, but they never resolved anything. I made the difficult decision to have him euthanized at a smaller, simpler veterinary clinic (the day after his last hospitalization at CVM, he couldn't stand, but he seemed to want to walk while lying down). At the smaller clinic, they told me that this was a sign of something wrong with his nervous system, and that if he had been checked earlier, the outcome would have been different. At CVM, they always told me it was a gastrointestinal problem and just took my money with tests and consultations. They treat relatively simple problems, but they don't have the slightest idea how to treat serious illnesses. Dermatology is very good; they tried to help me as much as possible, but Internal Medicine... it's heartbreaking. The staff caring for him during his last hospitalization didn't provide the care prescribed by dermatology, and they returned him to me in worse condition than his skin problem had been. They never answered questions and treated my dog ​​badly simply because he had a skin infection and, to them, he wasn't as cute as the other dogs. I repeat, they have absolutely no idea how to treat dogs with serious illnesses.
Those who treated him and didn't care about a life were:
Aida Roque Panchi
Mayra Lázaro
Claudia Morales

The only ones who cared about my baby were:
Galia Sheinberg Waisburd (an excellent dermatologist)
And Dr. Isai in the emergency room
Excellent veterinary hospital, they have saved two of my pets and the service is good, the care is also good, it is not cheap but it is worth it, I recommend it.
Thank you so much for your review.

We're sorry your experience didn't meet your expectations.

Thank you for sharing your feedback, as it helps us identify areas for improvement.
We'd like to learn more about your experience and review your case in detail. Please contact us through our Customer Service email: sguerrero@centroveterinariomexico.mx, where we'll be happy to address your comments directly.
Thank you so much for sharing your review with us.
Poor organization
Terrible service
Terrible organization

They don't answer the phone! It's a real shame because the quality of medical care is outstanding, but the secretaries never answer calls; they either hang up or let them ring until they disconnect. They're killing the business.

My experience at the hospital was bad; I was always attended to by different people, the information was incomplete and delayed, they didn't even know my dog's age even though her file had just been updated, long waiting times, zero tact, high costs, they discharged her and when I got home she started with diarrhea.
Specialized and very good. A bit pricey, but worth it.
It's a good center, but the medical staff has a terrible attitude; they treat patients reluctantly.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE

Last week I took my dog ​​in because of a problem, and they gave him pain medication, but he didn't get better.
Today I took him back, and they told me they couldn't find anything wrong and that I had to take him to a dermatologist.

My dog ​​was still in pain, so I took him to another vet. They immediately diagnosed him with an anal gland infection, treated his wound, and prescribed antibiotics. He's already improved.

BEWARE: THEY'RE JUST TRYING TO GET MONEY, and the staff are rude and abusive.

Excellent gastroenterology service with Dr. Mayra. In other places, I've had many tests done without improvement. So far, two of my little ones are doing well. The prognosis and recovery time were explained to me, so this also gives me confidence and I know what to expect.
You need to be on top of the reception girls
Excellent service

My experience at this hospital was deeply disappointing. Their processes are excessively bureaucratic, disorganized, and not at all customer-oriented. On multiple occasions, I felt I was dealing with an institution indifferent to the experience of its patients and their families, rather than a veterinary hospital that should prioritize care, empathy, and support.

THEY CHARGE LIKE ANGELES AND TREAT YOU LIKE THE IMSS (Mexican Social Security Institute).

What's most concerning is that there seems to be a culture completely closed to feedback. It doesn't matter if the comment is shared with doctors, receptionists, supervisors, or even via WhatsApp: the constant reaction is to become defensive, as if any observation were a personal offense, instead of listening, analyzing, and using the feedback to improve, as is expected of any serious service organization.

I even tried to respectfully share my experience with Dr. Elba Estrever regarding the organizational problems I encountered. Far from finding openness, I ended up being reprimanded for expressing my dissatisfaction, and the conversation ended abruptly, leaving me talking to myself. This situation confirmed my impression that customer feedback is neither valued nor considered an opportunity for improvement. There is also no adequate follow-up or humane treatment.

At no point did I feel supported during the process; on the contrary, I felt treated like just another number. I requested assistance completing my insurance paperwork due to the significant expenses I've incurred, and yet I was the one who had to follow up every 24 hours to ask if the documents were ready, without receiving clear information about delivery times or when I could pick them up. This is even more disappointing considering it's a veterinary health service, and a high-cost one at that. When a family entrusts their pet's health to an institution like this, they expect professionalism, organization, empathy, and a willingness to listen. Unfortunately, my experience was the exact opposite.

In conclusion, the human touch at this hospital leaves much to be desired. Customer service, communication, follow-up, and openness to feedback are practically nonexistent. The only part of the process that seems to work efficiently is billing. If I could rate the human qualities, my assessment would be below zero. Look for a better place.
At the kitten clinic, they gave my kitten the best care. They always kept in touch to give updates on how he spent the night or how his treatment was progressing.
Excellent facilities and well-trained staff

We came here because my dog ​​had an emergency; she was hospitalized for two days, and they kept me informed about everything. The doctors explain everything in detail, and the facilities are very nice. Thank you for taking care of my dog ​​❤️

The doctors are great, and all the staff are very kind and willing to answer all your questions about your pets. It's definitely a bit pricey, but they will definitely find a solution for your pets' care. I took my 13-year-old Chihuahua there for mammary gland removal surgery—it was a radical mastectomy—and everything went well. It's definitely worth the expense.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS CLINIC. NEGLIGENT.

We took my dog ​​to this clinic, and he was seen by two different veterinarians. Both times, they gave him a misdiagnosis, resulting in two incorrect treatments. They ran lab tests, and even seeing how serious my dog's condition was, they scheduled an appointment for five days later. We took him to the emergency clinic the day after the tests, and they told me he had liver and kidney failure, as well as advanced anemia. They prescribed special food and some powders. They gave him a maximum of four weeks to live, regardless of the treatments they suggested, which included either human medication or a blood transfusion. In just four days, he deteriorated considerably to the point where he refused to eat or drink. I went to another veterinarian for a second opinion, and he confirmed that the kidney and liver failure was due to a severe throat infection that his body couldn't handle. This was the reason we had taken our dog there in the first place, and they treated it as an allergy. Two weeks and two more appointments, and they never even properly examined his throat. The new vet did what he could, but it was too late. Between appointments, tests, medications, and special food, not to mention the time and travel, it cost over $15,000 pesos.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND this place. It's incredibly unethical to profit from our pets' health. To make matters worse, the people who attended to him and signed the prescriptions weren't any of the names printed on them.

Money is the least of our worries, even if we had spent more, as long as we still had our Chaparro with us. And that's not even mentioning the physical and, above all, emotional toll of seeing him suffer.

My dog ​​was admitted in very serious condition with a guarded prognosis. Thanks to the work and immediate attention of Dr. Fernanda Razo, who immediately identified my dog's problems, he was discharged today. The same praise is due to nephrologist Julio, whom I didn't meet in person, but who explained everything to me over the phone with great compassion, professionalism, and patience. I am truly grateful to all of them and everyone who was there, from the doctors to the cleaning and feeding staff. It's an expensive hospital, but it's worth every penny. In a country where justice existed, all living beings should receive this quality of healthcare.
I've had three generations of dogs going to this vet and I highly recommend it. It's gotten quite expensive, but they've never given me a wrong diagnosis.

Like everything, there are good and bad experiences. Because it's a place for exotic animals, we decided to take our rabbit there. But they don't give a clear diagnosis. First, they say everything is fine but more tests are needed. By the third day, everything is worse, requiring a CT scan that costs around $3,000 to find out what's wrong. Days go by, and now it's getting worse. When I took a rabbit there before, they didn't even give me the test results to show if they'd even done them. I've taken my cats to another clinic, and they give me the test results; here, nothing. I don't know if there's a lack of communication with the doctors, or if they don't follow up with the animals, or if they're just in it for the money. Because, as I said, in my first experience, my rabbit died, and the bill was unimaginable. All I got was the receipt, no test results, and they never gave me a proper diagnosis. And in this second case, where we're giving them another chance, it's the same. I'm sure the rabbit will die, even though we took her in time. That's for sure. I'll pay around 13 or 15 thousand pesos just to be told I'm still unwell. Anyway, good for those who had a good experience there, but I'm not going back. I hope the hospital owner has more oversight of the quality of service and care provided by his staff.

The cardiology facilities and service were excellent, however, our experience with Dr. Marleny in ophthalmology left much to be desired. She had zero empathy and a rude, arrogant attitude when answering our questions. We definitely won't be returning to her.
Very empathetic, the doctors explain things well, and all the staff are very friendly.
Excellent physiotherapy and rehabilitation care.

I chose this hospital because my dogs are 10 years old, and I was looking for a place that would give me confidence, security, and support for their dental procedure under anesthesia. Precisely because of their age, I didn't take this decision lightly.

The procedure cost approximately $12,000 pesos for both of them. However, my main complaint isn't the cost or the procedure itself, but the lack of post-operative follow-up and the terrible communication after I got them back.

Hours after the surgery, both dogs were lethargic, refused to drink water, one of them wouldn't eat, they were bleeding, and neither had urinated. They were also prescribed antibiotics to start that same night, so I needed clear guidance on how to proceed. I tried contacting the relevant department and only received automated messages, administrative responses, and were transferred between different numbers.

I specifically asked if it was normal for them not to urinate, if the bleeding was expected, how I should administer the antibiotic if they weren't eating, and if they had been given a gastric protector during the procedure. I didn't receive a clear clinical answer or a follow-up call. The response was that the doctor had already finished her shift and that my messages would be forwarded.

I understand that doctors have schedules, but if a hospital performs procedures with anesthesia and dental extractions on geriatric patients, it should have a proper post-operative follow-up protocol or someone trained to provide guidance for immediate questions.

As an owner, I wasn't looking for special or excessive attention; I wanted to know if the signs my dogs were exhibiting were normal or if I should take them for a check-up. The lack of a timely response caused unnecessary anxiety at a delicate time.

I'm left with the impression that, once the procedure was finished and I paid, there was minimal interest in my dogs' condition. When you go to a veterinary hospital, you don't just pay for surgery; you also expect support, communication, and accountability in follow-up care. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.

I see many negative comments about this place. For me, it was the best experience I could have had. I went there for an oncology appointment, and my dog ​​Kira received excellent care from the oncologist, Ana Pau. She made me feel comfortable and empathized with the pain I felt when she gave me her diagnosis. At no point did she try to take my money or perform unnecessary procedures. She guided me on how to make the decision about euthanasia and provided palliative treatment for Kira's cancer.

I deeply regret not finding her sooner; perhaps the cancer wouldn't have been so devastating for my princess.
That's what I consider a problem: even if you need an appointment as soon as possible, they schedule it up to two weeks later. Also, the people managing WhatsApp keep transferring you from one number to another. As for the facilities, the place feels comfortable and has everything necessary to care for your pet.
They accept credit and/or debit card payments.

My experience at this hospital was grossly negligent. I walked my dog ​​in; after examining her, the vet recommended hospitalization for kidney failure. I trusted them. It was three days of unnecessary suffering: she didn't receive the proper treatment, the correct nutrition, or the dignified care a geriatric dog deserves.
During her stay, different veterinarians attended to her without coordination, contradicting each other and showing no empathy whatsoever for her or me. They acted slowly while her condition worsened.
I made the decision to take her out of the hospital carrying her because she could no longer stand on her own—something that shouldn't have happened under professional care. The lack of ethics, coordination, and humanity of this team cost my dog ​​her life. I do not recommend this hospital.
It is a place with excellent service and ethical and professional care, accurate in diagnosis and treatment.

Excellent medical care, with one important suggestion 🐾

We took our dog to Centro Veterinario México (CVM) for rehabilitation after elbow arthroscopy for dysplasia, and the medical care she received was truly top-notch. Doctors Adriana, Regina, and Cynthia are an exceptional team: professional, attentive, and their approach to patients and their owners inspires confidence from the very first moment.

However, at a crucial point in her rehabilitation—when a hydrotherapy treadmill is needed to promote muscle development—we discovered that CVM doesn't have this equipment, which forced us to look for another clinic to continue her treatment. It was a difficult decision because the rest of the service has been excellent.

We hope that in the future they will consider adding hydrotherapy equipment. With the level of medical care they already provide, it would be a comprehensive service that would make all the difference for patients in rehabilitation. Their team and patients certainly deserve it!

Irresponsible and rude. First, they wouldn't discharge him because of the diarrhea, and then they wanted me to take him home like that, with watery stools. When I asked, the doctor even rolled her eyes at me. Completely lacking in empathy. I took him to another hospital, and they diagnosed him correctly there. And they gave him back to me filthy after so many days in the hospital. I DO NOT RECOMMEND THEM.

My puppy was dying. At reception, they weren't concerned about how he arrived until I told them he was sick. I had him hospitalized because Dr. Fernanda told me she would try to stabilize him and run several tests, which, according to her, showed nothing. My dog ​​died in the early morning without us knowing exactly what was wrong with him.

The next day, I went back to clarify the situation and find out what had happened. The doctor told me a possible cause of death up to that point. They never told me he was about to die, and they claimed to have called many times, which were obviously lies. Unfortunately, my dog ​​died, and the helplessness will continue. They're certainly quick to charge, though, and I spent over 9,000 pesos in a single day.

My experience at this hospital was very disappointing. The treatment I received left much to be desired, and on several occasions, I felt a lack of empathy and attention to my concerns. The most frustrating aspect was the poor communication throughout the entire process; obtaining clear information about my pet's condition and the next steps was difficult and generated a great deal of uncertainty.

When you go to a veterinary hospital, you look for trust, guidance, and support, especially in delicate situations. Unfortunately, that was not my experience. I regret choosing this place and believe they have a great opportunity to improve both their customer service and their communication with pet owners.

The place is expensive, and for what they offer, it's like going to the IMSS (Mexican Social Security Institute) for pets—they do you a favor by extending the treatment to line their pockets. Not recommended at all.
Among the best in veterinary medicine in all of Mexico.
Thank you!! Excellent service! Thank you
It's very good, they helped my dog ​​recover, the bad thing is that when you call, it's difficult to get an answer
Beware of oncology care; they don't have specialized doctors. Please request a different recommendation at another hospital.
They have highly qualified veterinarians with specialists. Excellent facilities with all the necessary equipment for top-notch care. Highly recommended 🐶 …
They lack empathy, they're only in it for the money and only focus on getting paid, not on the customer's well-being :(

I work as a pet-friendly taxi driver. I took a client to a vet clinic for her dog, and they returned him in worse condition than when she dropped him off. He was hospitalized for two days, we went to pick him up, and he couldn't hold on any longer; he died the next day. They hadn't even given him food.
They're just a money grab, and because of them, I lost my dog. The pain is indescribable, and they act like they don't care (they don't care).

NEGLIGENCE BY OMISSION AND CLINICAL MISMANAGEMENT: READ BEFORE BRINGING YOUR PETS, ESPECIALLY IF THEY ARE SENIOR.

I am not the first person to experience this; there are more comments that support the lack of professionalism at this clinic. I am writing this to warn other pet owners. They may be competent at processing lab results, but a good diagnosis without proper treatment does not save lives. I paid $17,000 pesos to learn that the hard way: by losing my 14-year-old dog, Frida.

Frida walked in, drinking water on her own and with a will to live, on May 16th suffering from dehydration and vomiting. She died on May 19th after deplorable clinical management.

Serious points supporting the negligence (I have lab results, invoices, and clinical documents):

Lack of specialization and judgment: I was seen by Dr. Claudia Morales González (a general practitioner who graduated in 2024, without a specialization). A complex case of a geriatric patient with severe renal failure (creatinine 340 µmol/L, elevated BUN and phosphorus) and documented pancreatitis from day one required a specialist immediately, not on the third day. She recommended hospitalization that could have been managed at home.

Complete omission of feeding (serious clinical error): Frida did not eat on her own. The standard and mandatory protocol dictates immediate assisted feeding. She went three days without food. They normalized her bilious vomiting by saying it was "due to inflammation," when it was caused by an empty stomach. They had antiemetics and chose not to feed her.

Fragmented care: Each visit on Saturday, Sunday, and Monday was attended to by a different veterinarian. Zero continuity, zero empathy; We were treated like just another bureaucratic hurdle. The treatment of a geriatric patient should be gentle and specialized; here it was cold and negligent.

Delayed and incorrect intervention by the specialist: Dr. Julio César Morales Soledad didn't arrive until Monday (the third day). He inserted a nasogastric tube, but instead of using it to address the underlying cause (feeding), he used it to drain bile (a consequence of fasting). When they finally gave her food, they gave her generic gastrointestinal formula, not renal formula, ignoring her primary diagnosis.

Voluntary discharge and delivery in a state of shock: Given the discrepancies and her deteriorating condition, I decided to discharge her. Without my authorization as her guardian, they removed the feeding tube. They handed her over to me in a state of shock: staring blankly, tachycardia, dry mouth, and unable to stand. In the phone call that morning, they tried to persuade me to keep her for another 24 hours to stabilize her, something they should have done since Saturday; they just wanted to keep collecting payment.

To pet owners: Don't trust blindly. Ask questions, challenge assumptions, and seek second opinions. Two independent veterinarians confirmed to me that the protocol for Frida was completely incorrect and that assisted feeding should have started upon admission.

Silence protects those who fail us. The way Frida was treated lacked medical ethics and the gentleness a senior dog deserves. Think twice before leaving a member of your family here.
Please do not bring your pets here

I took my pet to that hospital in Horcones on a recommendation, and my experience was frustrating and disappointing. I was supposed to see a specialist, but the treatment was cold and disregarded, with no regard for how I wanted to be treated. They never gave me a diagnosis, always saying that further tests were needed. Many lab and imaging studies were performed, for which I was given a price, but the price increased at the register. My appointments were poorly scheduled, resulting in inconsistent care, and worst of all, the negligence with which they treated my little one. They prescribed medications that caused severe allergies and side effects that were deteriorating my dog, putting his life at risk. Be careful with the care at this hospital, as their elitist, negligent, and indifferent attitudes do not lead to the good service they boast about. Fortunately, I arrived with a good veterinarian who was able to save my little one. Be very careful, and that hospital is definitely not a good one. VERY AWFUL
Terrible place. We took some kittens in and they returned them in worse condition than when we arrived. Not recommended at all; they know nothing about cats.

The service I received when making an appointment was terrible; they never have availability, and the answer was always the same: "There are no appointments available, come without an appointment and we'll see you when there's space."

I waited over a month for an appointment for one of my dogs, for a condition we already knew required surgery, which had already been evaluated. All of this was to tell me that surgery was necessary and give me a date for it. Of course, I was charged for this, even though everything could have been done during the first appointment.
So far, all the veterinarians who have treated us have been excellent.
In my opinion, Centro Veterinario México is the best veterinary hospital in Mexico City. They have a team of highly professional veterinarians specializing in various diseases.
Excellent service 🙂! …
Not recommended at all. They don't respect schedules, they charge too much for the service they provide, the doctors are completely uninvolved, and they treat patients like just another pet.
This hospital has always provided excellent care for my dogs; they have the specialties I've needed, and the doctors have been very professional, giving us the correct diagnosis and treatment.

Very expensive. It used to be a great option because they gave you results quickly and had all the equipment, but it wasn't as expensive. Now it costs between 3,000 and 5,000 pesos. A consultation was 850 pesos, I think, and I paid 3,500 pesos for blood tests and an ultrasound.

The hospital has good facilities, it's like a human hospital, and they charge more than for humans. Unfortunately, I didn't have a good experience. Dr. Aida Fernández did blood tests on my dog ​​and concluded that back pain was what was making her lethargic. She prescribed medication in doses too low for her weight. It didn't occur to her to make a diagnosis, but simply to mask the problem with painkillers and anti-inflammatories. That cost 4,000 pesos. The same amount I paid at the very professional Durango Hospital for ultrasounds and x-rays to diagnose spongiosum, including a very detailed medical examination of her entire body. It's terrible how they profit from the health of pets.
Excellent hospitalization service, gastroenterology and physiotherapy services!
Thank you so much for your review.
Excellent service

Excellent hospital, they treat animals well, it's fast, the veterinary medical technology is good, they have less invasive laparoscopic options (more expensive, but worth it). I took my dog ​​and now my cat, and they're very well cared for, which is what's important, and for us too.
Good service
Good care for dogs, meticulous check-up, very popular, appointment recommended.

My dog ​​got sick in February. She started vomiting blood, lost her appetite, and had diarrhea. They asked if she had eaten certain foods, taken any medications, or had any previous illnesses, and we said no. They only did one test, a blood count, and nothing else. They concluded she had a gastric ulcer, prescribed medication, and she was on it for a month. She showed signs of improvement, and it was time for her follow-up appointment. They told us everything was fine, but it was very strange that her ulcer hadn't healed. She relapsed because she developed bronchitis from aspirating something. They prescribed medication, but the diagnosis of her ulcer remained the same. They kept telling us it was a very rare case and that no doctor knew what to do. Nala continued to worsen; she wasn't improving. Two weeks later, she relapsed and was hospitalized. They still didn't do any tests other than a blood test and prescribed more medication for her "ulcer." She didn't want to eat, complained a lot, and we didn't know what to do anymore. A week later, she relapsed again and was hospitalized all day. They did an ultrasound and discovered something "strange" in her kidney. They told us it wasn't that serious, that we should focus on her eating and continuing to heal. A week later, Nala relapsed completely. That day, I decided to transfer her to a different hospital. There, they diagnosed her with a tumor in her intestine, stage 2 kidney failure, and said surgery was necessary because the tumor was constantly growing. During her operation, they discovered a tumor on her tongue. They told us that she had never actually had a "gastric ulcer," and that the constant medication she had been prescribed for those three months could only have been a significant factor in her kidney failure. Nala passed away three days ago from post-surgical kidney complications, and her "tumors" turned out to be cancerous.

Our experience at Centro Veterinario México was "good," all things considered, but there was a lot of negligence on the part of their veterinarians. They never conducted a thorough investigation, couldn't explain her illness, and didn't perform any further tests to check and determine what was actually wrong. Their misdiagnosis ended up harming my pet even more than she already was. I don't hold them responsible for my puppy's death because if that's how it was meant to be, it was going to happen one way or another. However, I would like them to be more thorough in their work. If they're told that a dog has a cough, they should make sure to investigate further and verify that everything else is also alright.
One of the best animal hospitals... yes, expensive but excellent.

I had taken my dog ​​to a neurologist appointment and everything was fine.

I had to take her back over the weekend to be hospitalized, and it was terrible.

- Before, during appointments, they had told us that with two seizures in 24 hours, we needed to take her to the hospital. We went when she'd had four, and they sent her home saying she was fine, that we should let the doctor know if she had another episode. I wrote to them, and they said they would tell the doctor, but there was NO communication. It took six seizures for me to take her to the hospital because the doctor never responded.

- They ran tests, and no one explained anything about the results or what they had done. Their only response was, "We stabilized her."

- We picked her up, and they just told us they didn't know if she had had a seizure, but that we should keep her and record anything that happened. How can they not know if it was a seizure or not?

- They told us she needs an MRI, even though in previous appointments the neurologist told us it wasn't urgent because she thought it was idiopathic due to her breed. If they had told me it was urgent, we would have had it done while she was hospitalized. Now it seems that if we don't pay for the MRI, they can't help us.

When we got home, we noticed her neck and ears were extremely red, and no one even came to let us know or say anything. All night has passed, and NO ONE has contacted us, even though I explained the situation.

It seems like they did us a favor, and we understand their job, but we at least expected a report from them with instructions, what they had done, and an answer, which we haven't received. I felt very reassured by this care, but definitely not anymore.
After the cost and the treatment you receive, it's unbelievable that they don't provide proper information and that they return my dog ​​to me all irritated and without answering.
Great human quality and professionalism from ALL staff, from the person who greets you, to the person who attends to you on your way out

A five-figure cost that doesn't grant you access to any post-hospital care other than continued payments.
After a week of hospitalization and delayed diagnoses, my pet relapsed on the third day after being discharged, and there's no one to help you, only the WhatsApp and switchboard operators, who either don't answer, divert your call, or are rude, telling you not to send so many messages, or leave you waiting for hours—or days—only to finally ask you to return for a consultation.
Their recorded phone message states that their primary interest is the well-being of our pets, but they don't demonstrate it.
However, they are always ready to collect payment. I've treated several pets there over the years, but it seems that the more they grow and open more branches, the more they lose sight of their goal of curing and providing timely care, and become more concerned with recouping their investment in facilities and the false appearance of a hospital with quality care.

My dog ​​was hospitalized for six days with kidney problems. During those six days, I was never able to speak with the nephrologist.

The care was superficial, but the actual specialist never showed up.

Good place.

We were referred there by Banfield because they didn't have the necessary equipment to follow up with her and get a more detailed diagnosis.

Her doctor was an extremely kind person who did everything possible to support her; however, the prognosis was poor. She helped us to give her the best quality of life for the time she had left.

They were also very kind to her during the euthanasia procedure.

We are very grateful to have found this place because they did everything they could for her.

The rating is due to their terrible telephone service; it's impossible to contact them. After four attempts and more than 20 minutes waiting for someone to answer the phone, I give up. I'm going to change veterinarians.

From the moment you arrive, the reception staff pay no attention. They don't bother to inform you if the doctor doesn't show up for your appointment; they don't notify you at all. And they handle the billing however they want, just because there's another hospital. They claim credit because you're not satisfied and don't care about the service afterward.
It's the best center, Dr. Julio Morales is an incredible specialist, thank you for taking care of my little girl 🙏🏻 …
The best doctors, the best facilities, but the reception staff and the person who handles inquiries via WhatsApp leave a lot to be desired. 😅 …
Excellent treatment of the kittens by Dr. Carolina, very professional.
Super friendly and attentive staff, both the care staff and the doctor who treated me, were very clear in his explanations!
They helped my dog ​​recover from pneumonia.

My dog ​​died due to a misdiagnosis at that hospital.
I followed the prescribed treatment, but then I went to another vet and we had tests done that were never performed at that clinic.
By then, too much time had passed since the first treatment, and our beloved dog died because of that misdiagnosis.

Unfortunately, I do not recommend this veterinary clinic. I do not consider them professional or ethical. On Friday, March 13th, they gave me a diagnosis and sold me several medications. On Saturday the 14th, I had to admit my dog, and they gave me a different diagnosis. On Monday the 16th, they discharged him, but on Tuesday the 17th, I returned to the emergency room, and they gave me yet another diagnosis and referred me to a gastroenterologist. I went to an appointment on Wednesday the 18th, and they gave me a new diagnosis and performed more tests. That afternoon, my dog ​​fainted. I only returned to the emergency room to request all the tests they had done. I paid for the tests and interpretation, but they only sent me images without interpretations, and not all the tests they performed. They just wasted my time and money. Seriously, avoid taking your pets to this veterinary clinic.

Only a few veterinarians have the tact to communicate your pet's condition and show empathy. Otherwise, the vast majority of veterinarians, especially the female ones, are terrible. They treat you as if they're doing you a favor. They give you half-hearted reports about your pet's critical condition, and on top of that, they mix up patients' test results. You can't be sure they're even your pet's; they excuse themselves by saying it was just a mistake when filling out the forms. If you have the chance to avoid this clinic, don't miss it.
Excellent service and attention from all members of this veterinary center.
Excellent service

I took my dog ​​to the cardiologist, they ran tests, and then they returned her to me with injured paws, claiming she was already limping when I brought her in perfectly fine. They refuse to take responsibility for her care.

So far the veterinary care has been good, the only problem is the customer service which takes too long because there is no direct contact with the doctor, in addition, Iara does not specify which branch to go to for studies or appointments.

Our overall experience has been very good. Everything is very professional. Many specialties. Very good doctors, with a high level of commitment. The prices, I consider, are about the same as in any other hospital. However, there is a point of distrust with some doctors who give exaggerated diagnoses and suggest euthanasia when it's not strictly necessary. It happened with a friend's dog; the doctor suggested euthanasia, and the dog lived another three years with a normal life, despite its ailments, but with its medication. Upon investigating, we saw that there's a group of doctors who run a company that provides at-home euthanasia services. Then we understood why they so often suggest euthanasia even when it's not absolutely necessary at that moment. My friend showed me the advertisement the doctor gave her for the at-home service. That's why we investigated. That's why it's distrustful, for example, to go to the emergency room and be seen by the "doctors of death." I only make appointments with doctors I trust. They should look into this issue. They need to be more ethical.

We had been taking our dog to this veterinary hospital for years, and she had always received excellent care. That's why we trusted them and kept coming back.

However, our last experience was very different and deeply disappointing.

We went recently because our dog had bloody diarrhea, a symptom that clearly worried us. During the consultation, the doctor also detected pyoderma, but we felt she focused much more on that than on the intestinal bleeding, which was the main reason for the visit. Although we shared several additional symptoms, most were attributed to her age (she is 16 years old), without a more thorough evaluation.

Blood tests were only performed because we suggested them. At no point were we advised to have X-rays or an ultrasound done, nor were we told that she might need hospitalization for dehydration or weakness. We left with a prescription for ulcerative colitis and took her home.

That same night, her condition worsened considerably, forcing us to rush her to another hospital. There, they performed a full range of tests and discovered she had multiple organ failure, as well as severe dehydration requiring immediate attention.

The most worrying thing is that, even at this hospital, her blood tests already showed highly abnormal liver levels, and yet we were told to schedule an ultrasound "sometime during the week," as if it weren't an emergency. We later confirmed that it was.

We fully understand that, due to her age, our dog is more vulnerable and that her condition could deteriorate more rapidly. But precisely for that reason, we believe she deserves—and ALL ANIMALS DESERVE—CAREFUL, UNBIASED CARE, TIMELY DIAGNOSES, AND, IF NECESSARY, PALLIATIVE CARE WITH PAIN MANAGEMENT.

We felt their assessment was primarily influenced by their age, which resulted in a lack of attention to detail and medical decisions that were inadequate.

Additionally, during the consultation, they referred to our dog as male on several occasions, despite her being female, which we also found careless and confusing.

Unfortunately, I NO LONGER RECOMMEND THIS HOSPITAL. It's sad to say, because in the past they were a place we trusted a great deal.

I hope this review serves as feedback to strengthen the medical training and, above all, the empathy of the staff, TO AVOID AGE-BIASED DIAGNOSES and ensure more comprehensive and humane care for pets and, especially, for their families.

It's the only place I take my rescued animals with parvovirus. Besides the facilities being top-notch, Dr. Mafer Galán and her team care for them like no one else. They have a perfect protocol, they know exactly what they're doing, they're kind and helpful, and it gives me a lot of peace of mind having them there. I know that if any of the more than 30 we've taken there didn't make it, it's because there was no other way. They do everything they can to help them recover. Perhaps the price is high, but like all veterinarians these days, at least this one guarantees excellent care.

It's unacceptable that it takes more than three weeks to deliver an ultrasound interpretation, and then the result is incorrect.

What's most concerning is that both pet owners and veterinarians rely on their service to make important decisions. In my case, the interpretation led to my dog ​​undergoing surgery that turned out to be unnecessary, as the diagnosis was wrong.

This not only represents a considerable financial burden but also an unnecessary risk to my pet's health and well-being.

This is definitely a service that should review its processes and quality control.

The hospital is excellent, with many specialties, and the staff is very attentive and professional. They thoroughly examine your pet, explain everything in detail, and keep an organized record. We've had excellent experiences with our pets every time we've taken them there. The prices are somewhat high, especially for tests, but it's worth it for everything they offer.
I was attended to quickly, it was a dignified treatment

My dog ​​needed an abdominal ultrasound, so I went to the emergency vet. They did a 4-point FAST ultrasound, and while it got me out of a pinch, that test doesn't warrant a written interpretation; if you want one, it costs extra. They told me verbally that it wasn't pyometra, but I'll have to get another one if I want more detailed information. The appointments for formal ultrasounds are very booked up.

Slow service, they issued a prescription that wasn't valid anywhere except where they sell it, I had to go back to have it made again and it took 40 minutes, the receptionist with heart-shaped glasses is a bitter person.

From what I've been able to gather, and after my visit, the hospital has a good reputation for caring for our canine and feline friends.
They are attentive and accurate in their diagnoses; if you need to take your pets there for care, this is a good place.
I've been bringing my English bulldog to rehabilitation therapy for a year now and he has improved a lot. He is 13 years old and Doctors Cinthya and Adriana pamper him a lot.
Excellent care from the doctors who are in the emergency room at night, my parakeet came in with its intestines outside and they gave us all the information to make a decision.

My experience was mediocre. Some veterinarians are so rude and incompetent that they shouldn't be allowed to practice. Ophthalmologist Marleni was only concerned with my dog's weight and referred me to another specialist without ordering any lab tests or anything. I didn't know that "fatphobia" existed in dogs too, and it's dangerous for a "veterinarian" to have it, since their diagnosis is completely biased because now it seems everything is the dog's fault due to its weight.

But the worst part is the receptionists—zero effective communication, zero problem-solving skills. A real nightmare.

There are some worthwhile veterinarians, but you have to know which ones. The care is terrible; they charge the same as a human doctor, but the service and treatment are awful.

Terrible experience. After two weeks of consultations and hospitalization, they couldn't diagnose a stomach infection in our kitten, even though we said from the beginning that he'd been vomiting and having diarrhea for days. They ran many tests but ignored that possibility. Another hospital detected a severe bacterial infection the same day. We wasted valuable time here. I don't recommend it, especially not with Verónica or Lucero.
The best hospital in every way: Love for your babies, care, knowledge, and technology

If you want information by phone, forget it! It seems like calling PROFECO (the Mexican consumer protection agency) here is a waste of time. It's easier to contact Banamex than to get a response here.
Excellent service, highly recommended

There are many hospitals, but this one has a whole multidisciplinary team of specialists to help animals, it has specialized areas for other species besides dogs and cats, it's the best of many I've visited!

DO NOT BRING WILDLIFE: YOU WON'T FIND HELP HERE.

My friend and I took a squirrel in poor condition to Centro Veterinario México hoping it would receive professional and humane care. We waited for over 30 minutes because we didn't have an appointment, which we understood; it was an emergency. However, when we finally got in, the consultation lasted less than two minutes. The veterinarian barely examined the squirrel, didn't listen to its heart and lungs, didn't check its ears or paws, and didn't do a complete evaluation. She just looked at its belly and said there was nothing more that could be done, that it was probably a tumor and that it was in sepsis, and immediately recommended euthanasia.
She told us it could be benign or malignant, that she didn't have enough information for a proper diagnosis, and that it would require days of hospitalization and a lot of expenses. As a student, I can't afford that.
We looked for other options, tried to find another place; we didn't take this decision lightly. Heartbroken, we agreed to euthanasia so she wouldn't suffer.

Afterward, they told us we couldn't take the body for burial, that it could only be cremated at an extra cost. The total came to $2,000.
Let me clarify: my frustration isn't about the money. I understand that procedures cost money. What hurts is the lack of empathy.
The consultation lasted less than two minutes, and they charged us $800. I wonder: aren't the people who work here supposed to love animals? Didn't that squirrel deserve at least a thorough checkup?
Even afterward, when they were about to euthanize her, they asked us how much she weighed, a question we couldn't answer because she'd never been weighed.
I left there with an overwhelming feeling of sadness, helplessness, and frustration. I felt we did the right thing by trying to help, but we found no support or compassion, only people trying to squeeze every last penny out of us.
If you find wildlife and are looking for real, humane help, don't bring it here. You won't find what you're looking for.

Hopefully, this experience will lead to improved treatment and sensitivity. No living being should be treated as a mere formality.
Excellent doctors

I don't recommend them. They constantly change diagnoses and medications, even when they cause adverse reactions. They injected my dog ​​with a medication that caused her to pant intensely and lose control; later they admitted it was a reaction to what they themselves administered, and yet they still charged us for the follow-up appointment. Little transparency, little responsibility, and zero trustworthiness.
They have excellent doctors, the downside is the administrative service; operators take a long time to answer and the same goes for clarifications.

My experience at this veterinary clinic was very disappointing. From the beginning, the doctors were rude and disrespectful to both me and my patient. I felt the diagnoses were given without sufficient certainty, and in the end, they turned out to be incorrect.

Communication is very poor: they rarely answer the phones, and the reception staff offers no real support. When you ask for more detailed explanations about the patient's condition or treatments, the doctors react with annoyance, which only adds to the anxiety of an already difficult time.

In emergency situations, the care is disorganized. I was informed that one medication had been administered, and later another person indicated that something different had been given, which creates distrust. Furthermore, test results take days to arrive, and you have to constantly insist to get them sent.

The costs do not correspond to the quality of service received. Overall, it was a negative and unprofessional experience. I recommend considering other options for veterinary care.

The clinic is very nice and everything is very clean, I won't deny that. There are also some attentive staff members. However, my experience with Centro Veterinario México was VERY bad and frustrating.
Some of the doctors are rude and completely unempathetic. When they deliver bad news, it seems like they're mocking you or responding sarcastically to your questions, which is unacceptable for those of us who are worried about our pets. They never answer the phone when you request information or results that have already been paid for. They take forever to deliver them, and when they finally do, there's no follow-up or a clear appointment to explain the results.
The handling of medical emergencies is the worst: first they say the patient is in one hospital, then another, then that they did transfer them… pure misinformation. One doctor said they had given the pet a certain medication, and another insisted they hadn't. They indicated that a test was "urgent" and simply never performed it. And the worst part: errors in diagnosis. We had to take our dog to another clinic, and there they confirmed that nothing they had diagnosed was correct.
It was a horrible experience and a very distressing one at a time of great anxiety. I hope they replace the doctors and staff who aren't performing well, and that the service improves with the good staff who actually show care and respect.

Terrible experience. If I could give it zero stars, I would.
The communication is agonizing: you call the numbers they publish and they only answer after many attempts, and when you're already in a critical situation with your pet, they answer whenever they feel like it. That's unacceptable in a hospital.
The treatment from some of the doctors was rude, cold, and tactless. Zero empathy, zero sensitivity. On top of that, they tell you they're "going to do" tests or analyses, they speak with certainty about things and decisions, and then you realize there's no clarity or consistency with what they supposedly did or what they promised you. It feels like total chaos, and you're the one who pays for the uncertainty and fear.

And speaking of paying: the fee is high for the actual quality of service and care received. The worst part is that in a life-or-death emergency, what you need is speed, seriousness, clear communication, and professionalism… and here, at least in our case, it was the complete opposite.

Seriously: be extremely careful if you're thinking of bringing your pet here, especially in an emergency. I wouldn't go back.
I appreciate the attention, professionalism, and dedication shown to our dogs 🐕, both during consultations and physiotherapy. Excellent 👌 …
Dr. Fernanda provided excellent care. The hospital has everything necessary for the care of dogs.

The service was terrible, starting at reception. They couldn't care less if your dog was vomiting. I waited two hours for the gastroenterologist and they didn't even see me again. It's a shame that this relatively new clinic doesn't even offer the minimum level of service that clinics in Cincinnati provide. They need to change their system, starting with the receptionists, because it's incredibly unacceptable. You can't even get an appointment for an emergency.
Excellent place with highly trained professionals
I always, without hesitation, entrust my rescued chubby girls to them. Please never stop doing your work with such dedication.

My experience was good with the staff's attention; the doctors were very attentive and treated my dog ​​very well.
The very bad thing is that from the first day they told me about two surgeries without any tests. Then the surgeries changed from pyometra to three types of cancer just because my dog ​​is a Bernese Mountain Dog. Tests were done ruling out cancer, but by then my bill was already over 40,000 pesos. My dog ​​came in for some skin wounds, and we still don't know what's causing them, but they keep quoting and scheduling surgeries. I think, or at least that's what they led me to believe, that they try to schedule surgeries for every dog ​​that comes in, since on one of our visits for follow-up appointments, two dogs left already scheduled for surgery. Personally, I wouldn't go back, since I went to a vet with a very basic office, and we already know what's causing those wounds for my dog, and obviously, it was much cheaper.

They call themselves a "Specialty" center, but they're not up to standard. The staff are very young, or lack proper certification, yet they still ask you to perform many tests and make incorrect diagnoses. They're overwhelmed, so the service is poor. A "urologist" was negligent; my dog ​​almost died. I filed a complaint, but they never contacted me.
Excellent service, wonderful veterinarians, and the prophylaxis area is superb; Dr. Paulina Cordero is a true professional.

Overall, it's a good hospital, just avoid the gastroenterology department. The veterinarians there aren't as qualified as those in the other specialties. We took our dog there a couple of times, and the results were terrible.

On the other hand, the rehabilitation department is very good.

I trusted them, and I honestly don't know if anyone will actually get a live cat from this place. The problem is they pretend to be a tertiary care hospital and claim to do everything, but in reality, they're neither honest nor realistic about what they can actually do. They do charge exorbitant prices for everything, bills in the thousands, and in the end, they give you back your cat dead. Don't ignore my warning.
Always great service
Excellent service, very humane, they take great care of the furry ones.
They are very professional.
They make a killing off animals. They don't respect the pet owner's decisions, just to squeeze in as many exorbitant fees as possible. Their service is pedantic and condescending.

Having gone to 6 or 7 vets to get the required certificates for re entry to the United States, I finally got lucky at Centro Veterinario México! The team were friendly and able to issue same day documents.

To be perfectly objective, their emergency service is terrible.
Indeed, as other users have mentioned, the receptionist greets you as if you weren't paying for a service, followed by a consultation that lasted less than 5 minutes. The doctor who saw us (Luis Luna) diagnosed "paralysis" without examining the dog beyond tapping it three times around the eye. No tests, no medical samples—truly an irresponsible diagnosis after less than 5 minutes of examination.

They gave an accurate and quick diagnosis for my emergency. A great place for emergencies involving unusual animals.

My rabbit (Brownie) came in as an emergency, and the service was excellent. Everything was done quickly—taking him to surgery, running tests, and everything turned out well. Now we just have to wait for him to be discharged, but I know for sure that in any future emergency, I'll come back to them. 🐇
They take too long to answer the phone and the ladies are not friendly at all.

One of the most unpleasant and inhumane services I've ever received. Dr. Jorge Fajardo had a terrible attitude, so arrogant that he wouldn't even listen to the person bringing the animal in and explain what was wrong. My dog ​​had a heart condition, and we took him in for follow-up appointments more than three times. The doctor always contradicted himself in the prescriptions, saying things like, "How can we give him that? We're going to kill him!" even though he himself had sent the instructions. My dog ​​is male, and he always referred to him as "she," meaning he never bothered to read the medical records. They never gave me the test results for my dog, and the final straw was when, at the last check-up, he told us, "I'll see you in January, well, if nothing happens to him before then, because this is terminal." We already knew that, but is that really the attitude of a veterinarian? Even as a person, it's deplorable that he would make those kinds of comments.

Don't waste your time or money on these people. The hospital is far from what it used to be and survives solely on its former reputation. After this terrible experience, I went to another cardiology hospital, and it made a world of difference.

It's regrettable that there isn't a regulatory body for these kinds of "professionals."

Despite the passage of more than 72 hours, they only sent one of the two lab results, and even then, without an interpretation. This is an urgent test due to my dog's condition, and they haven't been able to provide the necessary follow-up. The service leaves much to be desired. I don't know if it's an internal problem or not, but the lack of empathy and sense of urgency was very noticeable.

I only received a response after going to the facility in person to demand the results and file a complaint. The service shouldn't be like this, as it had already been five days instead of three.

I went there based on a recommendation, but the experience was completely unsatisfactory.

It took them ages to give us the results of an electrocardiogram and echocardiogram. The delivery was supposed to be within 72 hours via email, but I had to come to the clinic in person five days later because the person who was handling our WhatsApp messages wasn't responding. This makes me question their document management system and their clinical best practices. How professional is this establishment? Additionally, I see they operate under more than one business name. How legitimate is this clinic?
Excellent all
Excellent care for my dog, the veterinarians who treated him were empathetic, accurate with their diagnosis, good value for money.

I took my dog ​​to the vet, and he was hospitalized for four days. They ran tests daily, and everything was fine. Context: Our kitten, barely a year old, had been rescued from the street and hadn't received proper nutrition. As a result, her weight and overall condition were that of a kitten who wasn't fully developed. However, we managed to help her thrive, and she was growing strong and happy.

When we took her to the hospital, they lacked tact and offered no explanation as to what might have happened, beyond mentioning that she had a spinal injury from the fall, which explained her lack of mobility.

Trusting them as experts, we were told that she "possibly had FIP," a degenerative disease in cats.

Without going into the bigger picture, they urged us to make the terrible decision to resort to "euthanasia" to avoid gradual suffering, both in terms of mobility and future complications. I WILL REGRET IT FOR THE REST OF MY LIFE!
